column1: # The people. One row per composer, tab-separated, and the source of truth for
# every name the site prints, sorts by or filters on.
# It exists because the corpus arrives from two places that disagree. music21's
# MusicXML has no composer field worth reading, so tools/works.tsv names people
# by hand; When in Rome's RomanText headers carry whatever the analyst typed.
# Between them the index once held "J.S. Bach" and "Bach", "Beethoven, Ludwig
# van" and "L. van Beethoven", three spellings of Schubert and two of Johanna
# Kinkel — 49 strings for 43 people, which makes a by-composer page impossible.
# Resolution is exact match against id, sort, display or one of the aliases,
# after collapsing whitespace and case. It is never fuzzy: an unknown name is a
# hard error naming the string, exactly as build_catalogue.py refuses to guess
# at a corpus path missing from works.tsv. Add the alias instead.
# `sort` files the name as a library would — surname first, so van Beethoven is
# under B. `display` is what a page prints. `period` is a judgement, and it is
# here rather than derived from the year on purpose: all 413 Bach chorales carry
# one placeholder year, and the When in Rome half's years come from a per-composer
# guess table. A period read off those would be a guess about a guess.
